journal: Regime read off SPY/QQQ: both trend-stacked above their 20/50/200-day SMAs and within 1% of 52-week highs as of 2026-08-14. Called it risk-on and sized three starter positions -- XLE (accelerating momentum, 5d return nearly equal to the whole 20d return), core SPY beta, and a smaller NVDA clip on a mixed near-term read (flat 1d/5d inside a strong 20d advance -- treated as consolidation, not distribution, and sized down for it). 41.7% invested, 58.3% cash, three names, well inside the 25% single-name cap and the 8-position ceiling. Every entry has a stop and an invalidation written down before the fill, tied to the moving average that defines the thesis rather than an arbitrary percent. Process note for the tool: the live dashboard (Macro, the Ticker Decision Table, Paper Desk) all serve data through 2026-08-20/21, five to seven sessions past my 2026-08-14 decision boundary -- a known, already-recorded harness gap (the as-of bound exists server-side but the harness driving this exercise doesn't pass it). I did not let it into my thesis; every figure I cited above came from the brief command's boundary-safe snapshot, not from what I saw on screen. Worth restating because it would be easy for a persona to get this wrong without noticing. Also found the sandbox ledger the dashboard renders already held a full prior week's activity (7 positions, deposit dated 2026-08-07) before I placed a single order -- not my run's book, which the brief correctly showed empty. Ignored it and worked off the harness's own state throughout. On the product itself: the new Institutions symbol search on /institutions and the reverse link from a Ticker page's 'Which tracked filers hold X?' button both worked cleanly and closed a gap I'd have complained about otherwise -- NVDA correctly came back with an honest 'could not be matched to a CUSIP, not evidence nobody holds it' rather than a false negative. Paper Desk's per-desk visibility checkboxes initially read to me like two of five listed strategies had silently failed to render; they hadn't -- B3-concentrated and C-trend are deliberately unticked by default because B3 is a subset of a wider card already shown, and the checkboxes make that a one-click toggle, not a bug. Filed nothing on either of those since both worked as intended once I checked.

Regime unchanged from session 1: SPY and QQQ both remain trend-stacked above their 20/50/200-day SMAs as of the 2026-08-17 close, still risk-on. Screened all four watched names for two-timeframe confirmation. XLE confirmed hardest -- closed at a fresh 52-week high (62.58), up on 1d/5d/20d simultaneously, with the 5d move (+3.99%) running at half the 20d move (+8.01%), i.e. accelerating, not decelerating. Added 12 shares to the session-1 starter, bringing it to 36 shares; post-fill weight came in at 22.97%, inside the 25% single-name cap with room to spare. QQQ initiated as a new starter (2 shares): confirmed on 5d/20d and above all three SMAs, but 1d was slightly negative (-0.16%) going in, so sized as a starter rather than a full clip pending next-session follow-through. SPY held -- still trend-stacked but 5d return is flat-to-negative (-0.05%), no reason to add, no reason to cut. NVDA held -- 1d flat (-0.07%) inside a still-strong 5d/20d uptrend, same 'consolidation not distribution' read as session 1, unchanged. Every entry got a stop tied to its 20-day SMA and an invalidation written before the fill: XLE stop 59.00 (below 20-SMA 59.39), QQQ stop 705.00 (below 20-SMA 705.82). Post-fill: 4 of 8 max positions, ,619.99 cash (36.3% of equity), well inside every mandate constraint. On the tooling, working the surfaces I hadn't touched session 1: /tax defaulted correctly to tax year 2026 (the year with actual activity) and read '13 transactions... no lot was sold, so there is no gain or loss to report' -- accurate, re-confirms a fix from an earlier run under its own finding_id. /wash-sales rendered a clean, honest empty state, same story, no wash sale exists yet since nothing's been sold. /activity confirmed the known sandbox-ledger contamination from session 1 (7 pre-existing positions dated back to 2026-08-07, my own book starting at the 2026-08-14 deposit) -- not re-filing, already recorded. /backtest's event-study tool worked well once I drove the Run button through a real .click() call (a ref-based click via the computer tool silently did not fire the React handler -- no network request went out -- confirming this is the harness's known coordinate-click gap, not an app defect; I did not file it). Ran XLE through 'close > sma(20) and close > sma(50)': edge was small and mixed across horizons (+0.8% at 1 bar, negative from 5 through 60 bars vs baseline), which is a useful reality check against my own momentum read -- I did not let it change today's sizing since the sample window ('1998-12-22 -> 2026-08-21') runs past my 2026-08-17 decision boundary, a new instance of the same lookahead gap session 1 found on Macro/Ticker/Paper Desk, now also confirmed on Backtest and Report -- filed as a new finding since the harness rejects reusing a finding_id already used earlier in this run. Also found and verified against source: /report/XLE's Facts table has an 'As of' column that is empty for every one of its 33 rows, including rows whose own label promises a date ('Current drawdown as of'). Read backend/app/report/builder.py: the Fact model has an as_of field, the frontend renders it, but none of the 39 call sites that build the fact bundle ever pass as_of= -- it's always the constructor default of None. Filed as a defect; it's exactly the 'every figure carries an as-of' standard I hold this tool to, and right now the one table literally named for it doesn't.

Held all four positions this session -- no orders submitted. Regime unchanged: SPY still trend-stacked above its 20/50/200-day SMAs as of 2026-08-18 (close 767.45 vs sma20 758.68, sma50 749.84, sma200 706.28), though 20d momentum has decelerated from 4.12 pct at session-2 entry to 2.56 pct now. Reviewed each of the four names against the process the mandate requires (regime, screen, size, risk) with the intent of actually managing the book rather than defaulting to hold: XLE -- still the strongest name on the watchlist, closed 2026-08-18 at 63.68, a fresh 52-week high, up 1.76 pct 1d / 4.51 pct 5d / 8.85 pct 20d, still accelerating. Position is already at roughly 22.97 pct weight against the 25 pct single-name cap, leaving only about 203 in headroom before the cap binds. Checked the paper broker source (backend/app/paper/paperbroker.py) to see whether the mandate min-clip would even let me add that small an amount: it would -- min_clip_notional only gates a brand-new position (order.symbol not in self.positions), not an add to one already held -- but I decided against adding anyway. A clip that small is not a real re-expression of conviction, just a mechanical top-up to graze a policy limit, and the round-trip cost (slippage, one more lot to track for wash-sale and tax-lot purposes) is not worth it for headroom this thin. Chose not to force the position to the cap; if the trend keeps accelerating and price appreciation alone pushes weight past 25 pct, that is a good problem and a real trim decision, not a manufactured one today. QQQ -- flagged at session 2 entry as a starter specifically because 1d was negative going in, with an explicit note to watch the next session for follow-through weakness. That is exactly what happened: 1d -1.69 pct on 2026-08-18, a second down day. Price (717.51) is still 1.6 pct above its 20-SMA (706.24) and 1.7 pct above the stop I set at entry (705.00), so not stopped out, but this is now a watch position, not an add candidate -- held, no action. NVDA -- sharpest single-day move of the three sessions, -2.34 pct on 2026-08-18, deeper than either of the flat weeks that framed the original "consolidation not distribution" thesis. Still above all three SMAs with 5d/20d both positive (+1.03 pct / +6.01 pct) and about 6.7 pct of cushion above the 205.00 stop, so treating this as a volatile day inside an intact trend rather than a break -- held, watching for a close below the 20-SMA (212.10) as the actual invalidation. SPY -- core beta sleeve, trend intact but decelerating, no reason to add or trim -- held. On the tooling: spent this session pushing on book management and edge cases rather than breadth. Portfolio (the page, not the brief) still shows the known sandbox-ledger contamination -- 8 positions including XLV, XLK, XLF and IWM that are not mine, priced at the close of 2026-08-21 (three sessions past my 2026-08-18 boundary) -- both already recorded, not re-filed. Paper Desk is a set of independent reference strategies on their own 100k sleeves, not an order-entry surface for my own book; confirmed there is no live order ticket anywhere in the app, which is consistent with the whole product reading a brokerage export rather than acting as an execution venue -- not filing this, it reads as the intended shape of the product, not a gap. Tested three edge cases: (1) typed a 31-character garbage ticker into the /ticker search box -- no client-side validation stopped it, but every backend endpoint correctly rejected it with a 422 naming the exact length violation, and three of the four panels on the page surfaced that real reason verbatim; the Institutional Holders panel did not -- it showed a generic "filings service unavailable, or this build may be newer than the backend" message for the same 422, which is simply the wrong diagnosis for a client-side input error. Filed as a new finding, verified against frontend/src/components/InstitutionalHolders.tsx lines 49-60 (a single catch-all branch for every status code) and backend/app/api/institutions.py:202 (the actual max_length=12 validator that produced the 422). (2) Started the same slow institutional-holders fetch on /ticker/QQQ, then hard-reloaded the page mid-flight: the page came back to a clean idle state with no stuck spinner and no leaked error, and a second load of everything else on the page completed normally -- reload-mid-action is handled cleanly, no finding. (3) Fed a deliberately malformed rule expression ("close >>> sma(") into the /rules tester: got an immediate, specific "Not valid -- expected a value, found >" rather than a crash or a silent no-op -- also no finding, this is working as intended.

Regime unchanged in direction but decelerating: SPY closed 2026-08-19 at 769.06, still trend-stacked above its 20/50/200-day SMAs (759.77/750.43/706.73), but 20d momentum has slowed to +2.90% from +4.12% at session-2 entry. Still calling it risk-on, not transitional -- no SMA has been breached -- but sizing nothing new this session. Screened all four holdings against the process (regime, screen, size, risk) with the explicit intent of managing the book, not defaulting to hold, per todays focus on depth over breadth.

XLE -- still the strongest name on the book. Close 63.58, up 1d -0.16% / 5d +4.18% / 20d +7.40%, still accelerating on the medium lookback and trading 22.96% weight, ~$150 of headroom under the 25% single-name cap. No new evidence to add (a clip that small is a mechanical top-up, not a real re-expression of conviction, same reasoning as session 3) and no reason to trim -- thesis intact, held.

SPY -- core beta sleeve, trend intact but decelerating in step with the regime read. No independent thesis to act on either way. Held.

NVDA -- 1d -0.99%, 5d -2.91%, 20d +2.59%, close 217.56 now only 2.44% above its 20-SMA (212.38) versus more cushion at session 3. My stated invalidation for this position was a close below the 20-SMA -- has not happened. Watching, not acting; a name that is merely closer to its stop than last week is not the same as a name that has broken it, and I am not going to pre-empt my own written invalidation rule with a discretionary exit.

QQQ -- sold the full 2-share position (order s4-qqq-sell-1), filled 711.73 vs reference open 712.09. This is the trim/stop the mandate has been asking this run to actually exercise, and the read is not a stop-out on price alone, it is a thesis invalidation: the session-2 entry was justified specifically because QQQs 20d return (+4.86%) was outrunning SPYs (+4.12%) -- tech leadership inside the risk-on regime. As of this sessions boundary (2026-08-19) that has fully inverted -- QQQ 20d +1.52% vs SPY 20d +2.90%, QQQ now the laggard on the identical lookback that justified taking it. Two down days since the fill (1d -1.69% on 08-18, -0.20% on 08-19) compressed the 5d return to -1.05%, and price closed only 0.44% above the 50-day SMA (712.98), which had been comfortably below price at entry. Session 3 flagged this explicitly as a watch position pending next-session follow-through; todays data was that follow-through, so I exited ahead of the mechanical 705.00 stop rather than waiting for it -- the reason the position existed was already gone. Realized result: basis 1441.14 (2 sh @ 720.57, session 2), proceeds 1423.46 gross / 1423.42 net of a $0.04 fee -- a small short-term loss, first disposal of the run.

Post-fill book: 3 of 8 max positions (NVDA, SPY, XLE), $5,043.41 cash (~50.7% of equitys $9,947.86), settled cash only $3,619.99 pending T+1 on the QQQ sale proceeds -- consistent with the mandates no-same-day-reuse rule, confirmed by settled_cash < cash in the close output. Equity is down $19.09 from yesterdays mark, mechanically from the QQQ exit crystallizing a loss that was already reflected in yesterdays mark-to-market plus one more session of drift on the rest.

Tooling notes from this session: re-tested finding institutional-holders-panel-mislabels-422-as-service-unavailable by loading /ticker/THISISAVERYLONGTICKERSTRINGXYZ and firing the holders button (verified the click reached Reacts handler via network log: GET /api/institutions/holders/THISISAVERYLONGTICKERSTRINGXYZ returned 422). The panel now reads "THISISAVERYLONGTICKERSTRINGXYZ is not a symbol this lookup accepts. Check the ticker and try again." -- read the fix in frontend/src/components/InstitutionalHolders.tsx:190-202 (describeFailure branches on status: 422, 404, >=500, and a generic fallback, replacing the old single catch-all). Confirmed fixed; recording under the existing finding_id per the backlog rule. Also re-confirmed the known macro/ticker/backtest/report lookahead gap is still present (macro page stamped generated 2026-08-23, series as-of 2026-08-20/21; QQQs own Decision Table showed MACD Histogram Turns Negative FIRING 2026-08-21, 0 bars ago) -- not re-filing, not used in todays sizing; every figure in this journal is from the brief commands boundary-safe snapshot only. Spent the remainder of the session on the sell/tax/lot-selection path, which no prior session in this run had exercised -- findings on that below.

Session 5, last day of the week. No orders submitted -- the book closes exactly as it opened: NVDA 5, SPY 2, XLE 36, cash unchanged aside from marks.

Regime and per-name review, run in full even though the conclusion was hold: SPY closed 2026-08-20 at 762.60, still trend-stacked above its 20/50/200-day SMAs (760.99/750.94/707.13) but decelerating for the third straight session -- 20d momentum down to +3.31% from +4.12% at the week open, 5d now -1.96%, 1d -0.84%. Still calling risk-on, not transitional; no SMA has been breached, only the slope has softened. QQQ, which I exited on session 4 for exactly this kind of deterioration, confirms the exit was earned rather than lucky: as of this boundary QQQ closed below its own 50-day SMA (710.93 vs 713.05), something it had not done all week while I held it. That is the clean version of a counterfactual this process rarely gets.

XLE -- still the strongest name on the book and the one that has been accelerating since session 1. Closed 63.75, a fresh 52-week high, up 0.27% 1d / 4.41% 5d / 7.36% 20d, trading 23.07% weight against the 25% single-name cap with roughly 190 dollars of headroom. Same call as sessions 3 and 4: a clip that small against that little headroom is a mechanical top-up to graze a policy limit, not a real re-expression of conviction, and the round-trip cost is not worth it. No new evidence changes that today. Held, thesis and stop (59.00) both intact.

NVDA -- the position with the least room left before it stops looking like consolidation. Closed 216.85, still above its 20-SMA (212.78, cushion down to 1.9% from 2.44% at session 4) and well above the 205.00 stop, but this is the third session running with a negative 5-day return (-3.75% now). My written invalidation for this name has been the same since session 1: a close below the 20-day SMA. That has not happened. I am holding to the discipline I stated explicitly on session 4 -- not pre-empting my own written rule with a discretionary trim because it is Friday and the position feels closer to the edge than it did last week. Feeling closer to a stop is not the same as touching one, and manufacturing an exit today would be exactly the kind of rule I wrote the invalidation to prevent myself from needing.

The unsettled 1,423.42 dollars from the QQQ sale settles today (2026-08-21, T+1 weekday from Thursdays fill) per the harness weekday-arithmetic rule and per the settle-date range Activity renders on that row. No new trade needed it, but I read it explicitly this session while checking cash headroom and it settling in step with this session date is the correct outcome.

Net for the week: three names entered session 1 under a clean risk-on read, one starter (QQQ) added and cut inside four sessions on a thesis that genuinely inverted rather than a stop-loss reflex, and the three survivors held into the weekend on process, not inertia -- every one of them still has an intact, dated, written invalidation that has not fired. Equity closed session 4 at 9,947.86 against a 10,000 start, essentially flat with one realized short-term loss on QQQ and the rest unrealized mark-to-market noise on names whose theses have not broken.

Now the second job, the one this last session was actually for: five sessions of using this tool as if the sleeve behind it were real.

What would stop me routing real money through it, in order:

1. The ledger is not isolated per book. My one and only sale this week -- QQQ, session 4 -- came back on /tax matched against a lot I never bought, dated three sessions before I opened the account, with a fabricated 22.04 dollar wash-sale disallowance and a position the tool still calls open after I closed it flat. I already filed this at severe under shared-ledger-contamination-corrupts-fifo-lot-and-wash-sale, and I am not re-filing it, but it is worth restating plainly on the last day: this is not a UI bug, it is FIFO lot-matching and wash-sale detection replaying a ledger keyed on a bare account string shared across unrelated books. A real single-user deployment with one ledger would not hit this specific collision, but the fact that the collision is possible at all -- that the tax engine trusts account_id alone to mean one book -- is not something I would want standing between me and a Form 8949 I sign.

2. Provenance has a real gap on the one page built to carry it. /report/:symbol has a Facts table whose entire stated purpose is that every number carries the engine that produced it and when it was current -- and the As-of column is empty on all 33 rows, on every symbol, because none of the 39 call sites that build the fact bundle pass the date. I filed this session 2 and it is still true. A tool that tells me it is careful about provenance and then is not, on the one table that exists to prove it, costs more trust than a tool that never claimed the discipline.

3. Live research surfaces (Macro, the Decision Table, Backtest, Report) have no session boundary and will show me data past whatever point I am supposed to be deciding from. This is recorded as a harness integration gap more than a production defect -- a live trader looking at "now" has no lookahead problem, since now is always the boundary -- but it means I cannot trust this tool for any kind of paused or historical review without re-deriving every figure by hand the way I did all five sessions, off the brief command rather than the screen.

What worked well enough that I would miss it: the honest empty and error states throughout -- a zero-disposals year that names its own transaction count instead of reading as an empty ledger, a malformed rule expression that says exactly what it expected instead of failing silently, a 404 that lists the real routes instead of a quiet redirect. The cash module would rather withhold a total than publish a fabricated one, and says why in plain language when it withholds. The statement export carries every caveat inside the document itself rather than leaving it on the screen. And the provenance chain is real, not decorative -- every row on Activity walks back to an import id and a source row, which is exactly the standard I hold a ledger to and exactly what let me catch the shared-ledger contamination in the first place instead of just being confused by a wrong number.

Where I adapted to the tool rather than the tool adapting to me: I did the 25%-cap headroom arithmetic by hand every single session for XLE rather than the app telling me my room to add. I cross-referenced the Activity page per-row settle-date range against the Portfolio page lump unsettled figure to know when proceeds actually cleared, instead of the summary tile just saying so -- filed today as portfolio-unsettled-cash-lacks-settlement-date, alongside a positive for the row-level design that made the workaround possible at all. And for the whole week I trusted the brief commands own snapshot over the live dashboard by habit, not because anything told me to distrust the dashboard in the moment -- a professional should not need an out-of-band source of truth for figures the primary UI is also showing.

Verdict for the trial: closer than it was on session 1. Cash, equity, transaction history, lot disclosure, and the statement export were the blocking gaps a week ago and none of them are gaps now. What is left is narrower and sharper -- a tenant-isolation assumption in the tax engine that a real deployment should not get to test the hard way, and a provenance promise that is true everywhere except the one table built to prove it. I would trial this again with a second account before I would sign a real 8949 off it, and that is a real distance improved from where the week started, not faint praise.
